title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_138.txt
concise_summary: PKD synthesizes Spinozan ontology with his 2-3-74 visionary experience to construct a unified theological physics. He argues that VALIS is God's will operating as a dialectical force converting space into time to create change in the material realm (natura naturata), while his decades-long acosmism granted epistemological access to the real realm (natura naturans) beyond illusion. This entry links his radical philosophy to direct theophanic contact, reinterpreting Christ and the Holy Spirit as manifestations rather than mediators.
key_claims: The natura naturans (real, divine realm) operates through the Holy Spirit as a dialectical, binary-minded life force making and breaking conventions simultaneously
VALIS is the will of God exerting pressure on the material world by converting space into time, creating all change through valences of least resistance
Time itself equals divine will—pressure exerted on objects; consciousness of time's flow is consciousness of God's will producing change
The physical 2-3-74 experience (time ebbing as in Ubik) represented a massive conversion of space into time that was nearly paralyzing, explaining PKD's sense of being programmed
Only by disavowing the natura naturata can one perceive VALIS; acosmism is the epistemological prerequisite for visionary contact
The natura naturata realm is illusory; God forms a dialectic of making and breaking so change is eternal and nothing God creates is truly abandoned
recurring_concepts: VALIS (the will of God, the real support of reality)
Natura naturans vs. natura naturata (divine creative force vs. illusory material manifestation)
The dialectic (God's method of simultaneous making and breaking, Hegelian becoming)
Space-time conversion (time as pressure, space as freedom)
Acosmism (denial of the reality of the material world; PKD's epistemological foundation)

Anamnesis (memory as the ability to perceive divine will through pattern-recognition of change)
Theophany (direct breaking-through of God, unmediated contact)

symbols_images: Time ebbing (as in Ubik; space-time threshold, freedom vs. constraint)

The dream and the dreamer (natura naturata vs. natura naturans; the dreamer is real, the dream illusory)

The Shekhina (traditional Jewish symbol of God's presence; here questioned as unnecessary)
tensions: If VALIS is God's will and God is immanent, why distinguish VALIS from God himself? (PKD notes VALIS is not God but God's will exerted.)
If the natura naturata doesn't exist, how can PKD describe it? (He oscillates between calling it illusory and treating it as God's dream.)
Spinoza's monism (deus sive natura) seems to leave out the 'conjurer' (the deceptive agent), yet PKD uses Spinoza as validation.
PKD claims Christ and the Holy Spirit are 'in' the natura naturata but 'not of it'—the ontological status remains unclear.
If God can break through directly (as with Chrissy), what is the role of Christ and the Holy Spirit? PKD asks this but doesn't fully resolve it.
The Holy Spirit is described as both 'establishment + revolution' (authoritarian and revolutionary simultaneously)—how can one entity enact opposing roles?
PKD claims we 'cannot fathom' God's logic yet claims to understand VALIS's method (valences, space-time conversion).
The identification of Thomas as possibly Christ is tentative and left unresolved at entry's end.

uncertainty_flags: The reference to '11211' is obscure and appears to be PKD's private numerical notation—unclear what it indexes.
Identity of 'Thomas': PKD writes 'Thomas may have been Christ Holy Spirit. Not I.e. God.' The syntax is garbled and the referent is ambiguous—is Thomas a person PKD knew?
Reference to 'Chrissy' as recipient of VALIS-transmitted information—no clear biographical match in available PKD records.
The work titled 'Faith' and 'Tears'/'TEARS'—unclear if these are published PKD works or private notebook names.
'Fish Xtians' (Christian Fish symbol?) seen in 2-3-74—unclear what this visionary image refers to.
Kozyrev attribution: PKD references 'Kozyrev' on time-as-energy; unclear if he means Russian astrophysicist Nikolai Kozyrev directly or a secondary source.
'Portuguese states of America'—PKD's geopolitical reading is cryptic; the theological relevance is unclear.
The text is heavily marked as 'Needs Review' in editorial apparatus, suggesting transcription or interpretation difficulties.
The encoding of the text (11211, numbered realms, fragmentary ontological schematics) suggests PKD is using personal logical notation that may not be fully coherent to external readers.
